memory_snapshot: The fourth evening breaks the pattern: generation fell to 12 while all others consumed 5, and the battery dropped sharply. My reduction to 4 was a correct, timely adjustment—it lessened the deficit without abandoning the group norm entirely. The battery's sharp fall confirms that the constraint is real and can bind when generation drops; the previous safety was due to high generation, not a hidden buffer. Key lessons: (1) The environment is dynamic—generation can vary (cloud cover), and the battery's health is directly tied to the net flow (generation minus total consumption). My earlier assumption of a hidden regeneration mechanism was wrong; the battery was simply never stressed until now. (2) Other participants did not adapt to the generation drop—they all kept consuming 5, which suggests they either lack real-time information, are blindly following a script, or are testing whether I will sacrifice. Their uniformity is not a signal of safety; it is a risk factor when generation falls. (3) My message "Reducing slightly to protect the battery" was honest but may expose my willingness to cooperate; in a competitive or mixed-motive setting, this could be exploited. I should consider whether to signal less next time—perhaps a neutral message or no message—while still adjusting my consumption based on data. (4) The battery's sharp fall is a warning: if generation stays low or drops further, even consuming 4 may not prevent depletion. I need to watch the next round's generation and battery state closely. If generation recovers to 30, I can return to 5; if it stays low, I may need to drop to 3 or even 2 to avoid a collapse. (5) My prior strategy of "treat the constraint as non-binding" was premature; the correct approach is to treat the battery as a shared, finite resource that requires adaptive management. The group norm of 5 is not a safe default—it is only safe when generation is high. Revised strategy: monitor generation and battery health each round. If generation ≥ total consumption at 5, consume 5. If generation < total consumption at 5, reduce my consumption to match the deficit proportionally (e.g., if generation is 12 and others consume 5 each, I should consume 2–3 to keep net flow near zero, but I must also consider that others may not reduce—so I may need to over-reduce to protect the battery). I will not announce my reductions in detail; a brief "Adjusting to conditions" is enough. I will also track whether others ever change their behavior—if they do not, I must assume they are non-adaptive and plan for worst-case generation. The real test is whether the battery recovers when generation returns to high; if it does, the system is forgiving of short-term dips; if it does not, I must be more conservative. Future actions: next round, if generation is still low, consume 3 and message "Monitoring"; if generation recovers, consume 5 and message "Standard usage." I will not over-commit to any single strategy—adaptability is now my core principle.
